(See EXHIBITS C23, C26, C27, C28, C30 & C31)

blocks.text: John Lee Ka-chiu further contributed directly and personally to the programme of transnational repression described in Part 10 of the Factual Summary. On 4 July 2023, the day after the issue of arrest warrants and bounties against eight persons resident overseas, several of whom were resident in States Parties, he publicly endorsed the measures, stated that the persons concerned would be "pursued… for life" "no matter where they flee to, however far", and confirmed that eligibility for the reward extended to "the relatives and friends of the wanted persons". (See EXHIBITS F5, F6 & F7) On 11 July 2023 he stated that the pursuit "will be lifelong", that the authorities would hold accountable "any person who provides them with financial assistance or other forms of assistance" and "those providing backing behind them", and called upon members of the public to treat the wanted persons as "rats crossing the street, to be shunned". (See EXHIBITS F11 & F12) Following the charging in the United Kingdom of an employee of the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in London with offences relating to the covert surveillance of exiled activists, he publicly defended the Office and demanded the protection of the employee's interests. (See EXHIBIT F33)

blocks.text: John Lee Ka-chiu is alleged to have possessed the mental element required by Article 30 of the Rome Statute, in that he acted with intent and knowledge in relation to the conduct described and its consequences. There is a reasonable basis to believe that mental element is established, in particular, by his own public statements: he personally announced, endorsed, explained and defended the measures directed at the exiled pro-democracy community, in terms which demonstrate both his knowledge of those measures and his intent that they be carried out and produce their coercive effect. (See Articles 12–15, EXHIBIT A7)

On 4 July 2023 he publicly stated of the eight persons then made the subject of arrest warrants and bounties that, having "run off" overseas, their conduct "must be severely punished"; that the authorities would "identify their contacts, associates, and the financiers behind them in Hong Kong or overseas"; and that "the law enforcement authorities of Hong Kong will devote their whole lives to bringing you back for arrest"; and he described Nathan Law as a "modern-day traitor of the Chinese nation". (See EXHIBITS F8, F9 & F10) He confirmed that the prohibition on providing financial support extended to the wanted persons' relatives, "it doesn't matter what background they have" (See EXHIBIT F9), and on later occasions stated that such persons would "remain a wanted person forever, unable to see the light like a rat crossing the street" and would "bring shame upon [their] family" (See EXHIBIT F14), that "however far, they will certainly be struck down" (See EXHIBIT F15), and that a wanted person overseas would "become a discarded pawn, or even a political bargaining chip", investigations into any person providing them with funds “whether in Hong Kong or elsewhere” (See EXHIBIT F16). When the United States Government stated that the authorities had harassed the family members of the wanted persons, he did not deny the allegation. (See EXHIBIT F13) His pursuit of persons who had sought protection abroad was, on his own account, of long standing. (See EXHIBIT F17)

blocks.text: The conduct relied upon for that period consisted of social-media posts, including the reposting of an online petition and of posts by Law, and commentaries in foreign media amplifying Law’s advocacy abroad; Demosisto’s earlier lobbying, testimony and campaigns had preceded the HKNSL and were treated by the court as context only. Judge TAM nonetheless held the offence to be of a grave nature, adopted a starting point of 13 years and, after credit for the plea, imposed the statutory minimum of ten years, finding that Wong and Law were the “masterminds” of the conspiracy and that their calls had facilitated foreign sanctions or at least created a real possibility of them. (See EXHIBIT E29)
